Thoughtful sermon, but a few key corrections for accuracy: Roe v. Wade was decided in 1973, not 1971. The SBC did pass some moderate resolutions in the ‘70s allowing abortion in limited cases (rape, incest, health risks), but they weren’t fully “pro-choice” as we define it today.
The Weyrich/Falwell/Moral Majority history has real political elements—yes, they mobilized on abortion after segregation lost steam—but framing the entire pro-life conviction as “really about racism” is a big oversimplification. Catholic teaching opposed abortion for centuries on biblical/theological grounds long before any 1970s strategy. Many evangelicals shifted due to fetal development science and ethics, not just politics.
This risks the genetic fallacy: judging an idea by its alleged origins rather than its merits. Worth digging into primary sources for a fuller picture!
Respectfully.
